title: Add serde serialization to Rust structs — 3 turns
description: Existing Rust structs need serde derives. Turn 1: add Serialize. Turn 2: add Deserialize with custom field names. Turn 3: add JSON round-trip test.

files.Cargo.toml:
[package]
name = "serde-example"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"

task_spec.prompt: The `User` struct in `src/lib.rs` needs serde support. Add `use serde::{Serialize, Deserialize};` at the top and derive `#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize)]` on `User`. Run `cargo test test_user_serialize --quiet` to check it compiles and the serialize test passes.
followup_prompts: Good. Now add `Deserialize` to `User` so the round-trip test works. Also add `Serialize` and `Deserialize` to `Address`, and add `#[serde(rename = "postal_code")]` on the `zip` field and `#[serde(rename = "country_code")]` on the `country` field. Run `cargo test --quiet` and fix any failures.
Run `cargo test --quiet` to verify everything including your custom field names. Fix any failures and confirm all 4 tests pass.
